messages:
Maria Perez: FYI — Large enterprise prospect is asking for explicit contract language around audit-evidence retention, BYOK handshake timelines, and an export SLA. They want this in the contract before pilot. Any red flags?
Sam Choi: Do we have a standard retention matrix to point to? they asked for 7 years. 
Laura Nguyen: 7 years is huge. SOC2/ISO usually reference 2-3 years for evidence, but legal wants 7 sometimes for regulated customers. We need to separate: (1) system audit logs retention, (2) customer-provided evidence exports, (3) legal-hold capability.
Pradeep Rao: From infra side — we can support configurable retention per-tenant, but long retention affects indexing costs. We should offer tiers: 90d (default), 3y (paid), 7y (enterprise with export only).
legal-bot: Suggest contract wording: "We will retain operational audit logs for up to X period; upon customer request we will produce a compliant evidence export within Y days." Avoid hard promises for indefinite storage. Also define forensic export format.
Maria Perez: Good. They also want BYOK escrow: customer expects escrow/escrowed-key handoff if key lost. Are we ready?
ops-sre: Short answer: we support BYOK for private deployments and KMS integration. For hosted, BYOK + escrow is a new feature — we can offer a signed key-escrow handshake but need product + legal to define the threat model and key rotation/rotation proof. Ops impact: key custody policies + HSM integration.
Sam Choi: For launch criteria can we list minimal must-haves? e.g. 1) per-tenant retention toggle, 2) export pipeline & schema, 3) BYOK handshake spec + rotation docs, 4) retrieval SLA (X days), 5) product tests and one pilot customer.
Laura Nguyen: Add: audit access controls (RBAC + audit trail of who requested export). Also evidence format JSON schema v1 and sample export in docs.
Pradeep Rao: Implementation notes for infra:
```
- retention_config { default_days: 90, tiers: [90, 1095, 2555] }
- export_job => writes gzipped ndjson to S3 (signed URL)
- export_time SLA target: 5 business days (pilot)
```
Cost estimate: ~10-15% storage growth for every tenant on 3y tier; indexing cost up to 3x if we keep searchable indices.
legal-bot: For evidence export SLA, recommend 5 business days for initial contract, with an option for expedited export (48h) at additional fee. Also require customer to sign an export request form to prove authority.
Maria Perez: Good call. For BYOK escrow language: propose we offer "temporal escrow" where we escrow a copy only after a formal request and notarized key-loss event; otherwise keys remain solely with customer. Legal, is that acceptable?
legal-bot: That wording is acceptable as long as we detail escrow preconditions and that escrowed keys are stored in a separate HSM with access logs and dual-authorization. Also list rotation and revocation procedures.
Sam Choi: Timeline ask from sales: pilot in 8 weeks. Realistic?
Pradeep Rao: 8 weeks for minimal pilot (retention toggle + export job + docs + one pilot customer) is tight but possible if we scope backlog: block out canary infra, export generator, docs, and legal contract appendix. Exclusions: full searchable long-term index and automated escrow workflow (these are v2).
Laura Nguyen: Can we make a launch checklist for the pilot (product + contract + ops playbook + sprint owners)? I'll draft.
Maria Perez: Please add owners: Laura -> product acceptance criteria + docs, Pradeep -> infra + export job, Sam -> pricing & contract appendix, Ops-sre -> runbook for manual escrow, legal-bot -> approve contract language.
ops-sre: I'll add a runbook stub with commands to generate the export and validate manifests. Example command: `./tools/export_evidence --tenant=TENANT_ID --since=2023-01-01 --out=tenant123-export.ndjson.gz`
Sam Choi: OK I'll push a contract appendix draft to the drive and link it here once ready. Can we meet Thurs 9am to finalize? :calendar:
Maria Perez: Thurs 9am works. I'll invite the prospect and include a technical readout. Thanks all :thumbsup:
